chunks: As for what al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the least act a man performs with a woman that makes her unlawful for his son and his father. He said: The boundary in that is sexual intercourse, whether apparent or hidden, that resembles touching the two private parts.
So it does not contradict the two earlier reports, because this report is contrary to the Book of Allah, while the two earlier reports are consistent with it.
Allah the Exalted said: 'And do not marry those women whom your fathers married.'
And He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And the wives of your sons who are from your loins.'
And He did not restrict it to penetration, so it is appropriate that the prohibition attaches to the contract itself.
With the understanding that this report is disconnected (mursal) and its chain is Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd from Yunus, and he is weak.

And Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh (may Allah have mercy on him) singled him out from among the men from whom the owner of Nawadir al-Hikmah narrated, and said: 'What is specific to his narration, I do not narrate it.'
And this is his image in terms of weakness; he is not objected to with his hadith, and it is possible that, along with his safety from that, there are two meanings.
One of them is that the intended meaning is that if it is from the father or the son, the intercourse is apparent or hidden, resembling touching the private part without a contract.

For that is the least that makes the woman unlawful for the father and the son, as we will clarify later, that whoever commits fornication with a woman, it is not permissible for his father and his son to contract marriage with her.

The second aspect is that the intended meaning by mentioning the woman in the report is the slave girl, because the slave girl does not become unlawful by ownership itself, just as the free woman becomes unlawful by the contract itself.
Rather, what makes her unlawful is penetration or what follows its manner, such as kissing, stripping, and looking at what is not permissible for non-owners to look at.
As we will clarify later, if Allah wills.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum act that makes a woman unlawful for a man's father and son in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi presents a critical analysis of a weak, isolated report (khabar al-wahid) from al-Saffar to determine the minimum act causing prohibition, ultimately favoring the view that the marriage contract itself renders the woman unlawful for the father and son, consistent with Quran 4:22-23. He offers two interpretive resolutions: either the weak report refers specifically to non-marital sexual acts (like fornication) which also create prohibition, or it applies to slave girls where ownership alone does not prohibit, requiring actual penetration or equivalent acts. This highlights the Shia scholarly method of reconciling seemingly contradictory reports by evaluating chain strength and contextual application to different categories of women.
